description:
The Son/Daughter Education Assistance Scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Uttarakhand Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (UKBOCWWB) in India.

This scheme was officially launched on January 1, 2019.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to the children of registered construction workers in Uttarakhand.

The scheme aims to support the education of children from economically weaker sections of society.

It specifically targets the children of workers engaged in the building and construction sector.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is intended to cover educational expenses.

The assistance is available for children pursuing education from the primary level up to higher education.

The scheme provides a fixed amount of financial aid based on the level of education.

For students in primary education, the scheme offers an annual assistance of ₹5,000.

For students in secondary education, the financial assistance increases to ₹10,000 per year.

For students in higher secondary education, the assistance is ₹15,000 per year.

For students pursuing professional courses or higher education, the assistance can go up to ₹25,000 per year.

The scheme is designed to alleviate the financial burden on construction workers and encourage education among their children.

To be eligible for this scheme, applicants must be registered construction workers under the UKBOCWWB.

The applicant must have a valid registration number with the board.

The children of the registered workers must be enrolled in recognized educational institutions.

There are no specific age limits mentioned for the children under this scheme.

However, the educational institution must be recognized by the government.

The income criteria for eligibility stipulate that the family income of the construction worker should not exceed ₹3 lakh per annum.

This income limit is set to ensure that the benefits reach the economically weaker sections of society.

The application process for the Son/Daughter Education Assistance Scheme is straightforward.

Interested applicants must fill out the application form available on the UKBOCWWB website.

The application form requires details such as the worker's registration number, the child's educational details, and family income.

Applicants must also submit supporting documents along with the application form.

Required documents include a copy of the construction worker's registration certificate.

A copy of the child's admission letter from the educational institution is also necessary.

Additionally, applicants must provide proof of income such as an income certificate issued by a competent authority.

Once the application is complete, it should be submitted to the local office of the UKBOCWWB.

The board reviews the applications and verifies the submitted documents.

Disbursement of funds is typically done on an annual basis.

The financial assistance is credited directly to the bank account of the registered construction worker.

The timeline for application submission usually coincides with the academic calendar.

Applications are generally accepted at the beginning of the academic year.

The exact deadline for application submission is usually announced by the UKBOCWWB each year.

It is advisable for applicants to keep an eye on official announcements for specific dates.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Uttarakhand Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The board operates under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of Uttarakhand.

For any inquiries or assistance, applicants can contact the UKBOCWWB office directly.

The contact details for the board can be found on their official website.

The scheme has been instrumental in promoting education among the children of construction workers.

Since its launch, thousands of children have benefited from this financial assistance.

The scheme has also contributed to reducing dropout rates among children of construction workers.

The UKBOCWWB regularly monitors the implementation of the scheme to ensure transparency and efficiency.

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the scheme further.

The Son/Daughter Education Assistance Scheme is part of a broader initiative to uplift the socio-economic status of construction workers in Uttarakhand.

The government aims to create a more educated workforce through such welfare schemes.

This initiative aligns with the national goal of improving literacy rates in India.

The scheme reflects the commitment of the Uttarakhand government to support vulnerable sections of society.

In conclusion, the Son/Daughter Education Assistance Scheme is a vital program aimed at enhancing educational opportunities for the children of construction workers.

It provides significant financial support to ensure that children can pursue their studies without financial hindrance.

The scheme is a step towards building a more educated and skilled future generation in Uttarakhand.
